Subject: SOC 2 evidence: admin activity export & delivery options

Hi Kimberly,

We're kicking off our SOC 2 evidence collection for Q3 and Carebridge would like to include Redwood's admin activity logs as part of the operator audit evidence. Can you help with the following so we can scope our evidence request?

- What admin/operator events are captured (create/delete/login/sudo/role_changes/etc.)?
- Retention windows by event type and how deletions/overwrites are handled.
- Export options: on-demand snapshot (CSV/JSON), scheduled bulk exports, and near-real-time streaming (pub/sub or Kinesis).
- Chain-of-custody / integrity: checksums, signed manifests, and transfer methods (SFTP, secure GCS/AWS bucket).
- Redaction options for PII and operator identifiers for shared audits.
- Expected delivery SLA for an evidence bundle and supported formats.

I've attached a short SOC 2 questionnaire and our internal evidence checklist. If easier, we'd like a short walkthrough next week and an example manifest/CSV sample we can include in the control narrative.

Thanks — aim to get this to our auditors by 7/20.

Ellen

Hi Ellen — thanks for the detail and the deadline. Happy to help. High-level answers inline and then a proposed delivery plan below.

What’s logged
- Operator actions: user sign-ins, API key usage, role/permission changes, role bindings, policy updates, service account creation, access grant/revokes, session start/stop.
- System events: instance lifecycle (start/stop/reboot), model deployments, config changes, autoscale events.
- Request metadata: timestamp, request id, actor (operator id), target resource, action, client IP, region, and outcome (success/fail).

Retention
- Default retention: 365 days for admin/operator events.
- Longer retention available (3 years) under enterprise/Private plans; can be configured per-account with retention policies.
- Deletion model: soft-delete with tombstones for 30 days before permanent purge; export scripts can include tombstones as a separate column.

Export options
- On-demand snapshot: CSV or newline-delimited JSON, compressed (.gz), includes a manifest with SHA256 checksums.
- Scheduled bulk: daily/weekly exports into customer-owned cloud bucket (S3/GCS/Azure) with server-side encryption (SSE).
- Streaming: near real-time via Pub/Sub (GCP) or Kinesis (AWS). We can provide a connector or deliver to your ingestion endpoint.

Integrity & chain-of-custody
- Every export includes a signed manifest (manifest.json) with per-file SHA256 and an overall bundle signature (Ed25519) tied to Redwood's key.
- Transfer options: SFTP (key-based auth), pre-signed S3/GCS URLs to your bucket, or direct push to your secure endpoint.

Redaction
- PII redaction options: operator email -> hashed operator_id, IP masking (first two octets zeroed), and field-level redaction rules. We can deliver a redaction report showing which fields were transformed.

Delivery SLA & formats
- Ad-hoc snapshot: 24–48 hours to generate and deliver a signed bundle.
- Scheduled bulk: daily exports delivered within the first 2 hours of the day.
- Streaming: sub-minute latency under normal load.

Proposed next steps (we can do all in parallel):
1) Kim to share a sample manifest + 24-hour CSV sample (attached).
2) Quick 30-min call to confirm which export mode you want and where to deliver.
3) If you need chain-of-custody packaging, we will deliver a signed bundle and checksum file.

I've attached a sample manifest (redwood_admin_manifest_sample.csv) and included Lauren for retention policy details and Markus for streaming connector questions.

Would 7/13 10:00am PT work for a call?

—Kim

Ellen — one small detail on retention that often comes up from auditors: the export manifest we produce includes an event_type column and a retention_hint column so you can show auditors which class of event was retained for what window. For your control narrative, call out:

- Admin operator events: 365d (default) 
- Critical security events (login failures, privilege escalations): 3 years by default for enterprise customers (we can extend)
- Audit snapshot retention: exports are stored in our staging for 30 days after generation if you need a re-transfer.

Also, if you want a hashed operator identifier rather than plaintext, we hash using HMAC-SHA256 with a per-account salt and include that salt reference in the manifest (so auditors can verify if you provide the salt).

I'll be on the call with Kim and Markus tomorrow.

—Lauren
